title: Human ECoG speaking consonant-vowel syllables
description: High-density (256-channel) electrocorticography (ECoG) recorded at the University of California, San Francisco from epilepsy patients reading aloud consonant-vowel syllables. The dataset contains 31 recording blocks from four subject codes, with hand-marked annotations of syllable onset, consonant-vowel transition and offset, and electrode anatomical labels. It is organised as iEEG-BIDS with byte-identical NWB files, and supports study of speech articulation in human ventral sensorimotor cortex.
methods_description: Cortical local field potentials were recorded with subdural high-density 256-channel ECoG arrays and a multichannel amplifier connected to a Tucker-Davis Technologies digital signal processor, sampled at about 3052 Hz. Participants read aloud consonant-vowel syllables (18-19 consonants followed by /a/, /u/ or /i/) from a list. Syllable timing was hand-annotated from speech recordings, and the microphone audio was removed from the shared files.
